build: intent-surface after the build manifest (studio as published 2026-11-26)
walk: Chrome, cold, localStorage cleared; 1440x900 and 390x844; open /intent, Try an example, scroll to the drawing, open mission control

F1.what: After Try an example, the drawing starts 2,248 px down on desktop and the intent map 3,130 px; on a phone the map is 5,209 px down (six screens)

F2.what: The example lands on a quiz: redline 1 asks what you are ultimately trying to achieve, although the example states its end in mind; the payoff is out of sight

F3.what: A stray progress-track line is drawn across the top bar, through the ZTHR mark on a phone

F4.what: Empty state contradicts itself: 'Step 1 of 6: Your words are in' and 'Open redlines 3' before anything is typed

F5.what: The example's readings are hand-written but labelled with the families gemini and llama, and the status says 'sample readings from two model families'

F6.what: Nothing on first open says who this is for or what you will get; redline, balloon, datum, gauge and ratchet are used without a gloss

F7.what: The intent map opens at 55% to fit the sheet column; card text renders near 7 px until Full width is pressed

F8.what: Mission control's headline reads '0 of 47 journeys pass' when nothing was measured, which reads as failure

F9.what: Question hints are ungrammatical, for example 'It decides choosing between ways of meeting it'

F10.what: After release, nothing shows what happens next: how the package reaches the factory, who signs its journeys in, and where the measure appears

F11.what: No link from any page to the source, the licence, the package formats or how to extend the lexicon, roles, catalogue or manifest rules

F12.what: On zthr.ai there is no model to read your words, so the two-reading path means copying a prompt into two other models and pasting JSON back

F13.what: Every part of the drawing opens a drawer with source, relations, open questions and the package file; the release preview shows every file and the build manifest every part

F14.what: Accessibility checks are clean in light and dark at desktop and phone; focus moves to the next question; diagrams have labelled boxes and a Parts list text view

F15.what: Your own words are quoted beside every interpretation, each statement says who supplied it, and 'Why this is asked' explains each question

F16.what: Manufacturing terms are used correctly: datum, balloons, title block, redlines, control plan, special characteristics, bill of materials with find numbers, make or buy, revisions with reasons

F17.what: The intake already reads Spec Kit, Kiro, OpenSpec, Gherkin and HTML, and there is a command line, but the page never says so

F18.what: Mission control shows intents, journeys and the factory side by side, but not the stages the factory runs (design, build, QA, release), and offers one level of view; you cannot see the platform as one system, intent in to software out

denise.voice: It quoted me back, which I liked. But I opened it and got a quiz about something I had already said, and I had to scroll forever to find what I was getting.

raj.voice: The traceability is the best I have seen. I only found it because I kept scrolling, and nothing told me it would read my Gherkin.

lena.voice: On my phone it was a text box and a long page. I never saw the drawing or the part list, which is what I came for.

tom.voice: The package preview and the hashes are real engineering. Then I saw sample readings labelled gemini and llama, and the dashboard saying zero of forty-seven pass. Which numbers do I believe?

aiko.voice: The drafting sheet is a real point of view and the map is lovely once you go full width. The first screen is a form, there is a line through the nav, and the best thing is three screens down.

grace.voice: Refusal journeys, a coverage matrix with red squares, tolerances as ratchets: that is how I think. I would like to see the card format documented so I can add my own outside the UI.

marcus.voice: Staff seeing student data became forbidden outcomes and controls on its own, which I rarely see. I need to know where my words go when I press Read with Claude, and where the package goes after.

priya.voice: Agreement between independent readings becoming fact, held-out personas, planted defects: this is serious. Which is why hand-written readings labelled as two model families in the example is exactly the thing I would write up.

sam.voice: In five minutes I saw a form and a quiz. Someone had to tell me to scroll to the build manifest, and that is the slide that matters: what exists, what is new, and how it is proven.

jordan.voice: Apache 2.0 in the README, data-driven catalogue and lexicon: good bones. None of it is linked from the app, and I cannot find a schema for the package or how to add a rule.

rosa.voice: Focus moves where it should and the diagrams have labelled boxes. At 200% the page is very long and the drawing is far from the questions it depends on.

kenji.voice: Whoever built this has worked under a document control system: the terms hold up. The sheet should lead, as a drawing does, not sit under a form.

keisha.voice: I did not understand what it was. A box to type in and a long page.
